projectServices.spec.needService: The service item needs a service: name, start command, port (working directory, environment variables, health check, autostart and web page as needed)
projectServices.spec.cwdMissing: Working directory {dir} doesn't exist (or isn't a folder): create it first, or use an existing folder
projectServices.spec.portTaken: Port {port} is already used by {holder}: pick another one
projectServices.rollout.notLinked: Ergo wasn't started by the service manager (not connected to the service manager), so it can't bring the service online for you: register it in the service manager by hand, or start ergo through the service manager and it'll catch up automatically
projectServices.rollout.unsupported: This service manager version doesn't support owned services, so register it in the service manager by hand (ergo catches up automatically after the service manager is upgraded and restarted)
projectServices.rollout.withdrawNotLinke: Ergo isn't connected to the service manager right now, so it can't take the service down: remove {app} in the service manager by hand (lsm owned remove)
projectServices.rollout.withdrawUnsuppor: This service manager version doesn't support owned services, so it can't be taken down: remove it in the service manager by hand
projectServices.outage.failed: The service manager reports it failed
projectServices.outage.offline: It's stopped in the service manager (someone may have stopped it there)
projectServices.outage.missing: It's no longer registered in the service manager (someone may have removed it there)
projectServices.outage.starting: It never came up (still starting in the service manager)
projectServices.outage.stopping: It never stopped or came back up (stopping in the service manager)
projectServices.means.label: The project's own service (run by the service manager)
projectServices.entry.url: Service “{title}” of project “{project}”: entry {url} (opens in ergo's built-in browser)
projectServices.power.notInUse: Project “{name}” isn't in use, so there are no services to start or shut down
projectServices.power.noServices: Project “{name}” has no services online, so there's nothing to start or shut down
projectServices.power.lsm.waiting: Can't reach the service manager; try again once it's connected
projectServices.power.lsm.unsupported: This service manager version doesn't support owned services, so ergo can't start or shut them down for you: do it in the service manager
projectServices.power.lsm.disabled: Ergo wasn't started by the service manager (not linked), so it can't start or shut down services for you: do it in the service manager
projectServices.power.stopFailed: The service manager didn't stop it (no reason given)
projectServices.events.noCredential: No credential: send the header Authorization: Bearer <value of the environment variable {env}>. This API is only for services launched from an operations plan; the credential is injected when the service goes live
projectServices.events.badCredential: Wrong or revoked credential: it is revoked when the service is withdrawn or the project is retired or archived, and a new one is issued when it goes live again. Read it from the environment variable {env} every time; don't hard-code it
projectServices.events.noWaiter: Nothing in the operations plan waits for the event “{name}”, so nothing was woken and nothing was spent. You can report: {names}. To report a new name, add it to the operations plan and have the user confirm it first
projectServices.events.paused: The task waiting for the event “{name}” is paused, so nothing was woken. Report again once the task is resumed
projectServices.events.rateLimited: Service “{title}” is reporting too fast: at most {limit} per minute. This one wasn't counted; try again in {seconds} seconds
projectServices.events.tooLarge: The data is too large: at most {max} bytes, so nothing was woken. Report only what matters and put the full text in a file for the owner to read
projectServices.tool.switch: Start or shut down project services
